orca: CLI on plain node as `orca-ide`/`orca`, six agent skills; GUI is `orca-ide-app`

Install Orca's CLI the way upstream's .deb lays it out: `orca-ide` on
PATH is the CLI, and the GUI is off that name (here `orca-ide-app`, used
by the desktop Exec). Orca's skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal
to run exactly `orca-ide`; master had the GUI there, with an always-on
--ozone-platform=wayland that broke the GUI binary's own CLI dispatch
("Unknown flag --ozone-platform for command: open").

The CLI is plain JavaScript, so it runs on nixpkgs' nodejs_24 (Electron
43 bundles node 24) as a plain exec -- no sandbox between the caller and
the CLI. ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE points `orca-ide open` at the nixGL-wrapped
GUI; NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as upstream's shim does.

GUI: the wayland flag only outside node mode (`serve` probes the GUI
with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and Node rejects it); dieWithParent off,
since the GUI that `open` spawns is the CLI's direct child.

Six skills (orca-cli, orchestration, computer-use, orca-per-workspace-env,
orca-linear, linear-tickets) from stablyai/orca at the AppImage's own
sourceCommit; tests/orca-cli-skills.sh holds them to the hashes in the
build's current-manifest.json and the rev to the sourceCommit.

Supersedes the orca-cli-skills branch, which ran the CLI inside bwrap
and needed a hand-written signal forwarder to stop `serve` cleanly.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+

+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"

+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }

+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }

+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.

+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi

+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi

+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.

+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"

+# which under plain node is node itself. Exactly the profile's GUI: the
+# unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too, minus nixGL.

+# `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a
+# script as argv, and Node rejects the flag ("bad option", exit 9).

+# --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment `open` returns.

+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi

+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)

+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done

+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi

+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')

+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi

+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }

+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)

+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done

+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

+app=$(sed -nE 's|.*ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-([^}]*)\}.*|\1|p' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")
+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# The GUI's --ozone-platform=wayland must stay out of node mode: the CLI's
+# `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a
+# script as argv, and Node rejects the flag ("bad option", exit 9).
+out=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -p '"node-ok"' 2>"$T/node-err")
+if [ "$out" = node-ok ]; then
+  pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "${out:-$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")}"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, then exits. Each GUI wrapper layer
+# execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the CLI's own child; with
+# --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment `open` returns.
+bash -c 'ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 3000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 4000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 &' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "payload died with its spawning parent"; fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: CI's bash is built without programmable completion.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }
+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+
+printf '\n%d/%d passed\n' "$((n-fails))" "$n"
+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
                     -c bash "$t"; then
                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
                else
                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            *)
              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
              rc=1
              ;;
          esac

          echo "---8<--- end"
          exit $rc

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

## Review: origin/master..HEAD (63f565eb, "orca: CLI on plain node as `orca-ide`/`orca`, six agent skills; GUI is `orca-ide-app`")

I read the full diff, the commit message, the six fetched SKILL.md files (`/nix/store/REDACTED/skills/*`), upstream's `resources/bin/orca-ide` shim, the CLI runtime sources (`out/cli/runtime/{launch,orca-app-executable,serve-app-launcher}.js`), `.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml`, and the skills wiring in home.nix (lines 2296-2329). I wrote nothing.

### Critical
None.

### Important

**1. The GUI-lifetime case passes even if `dieWithParent = false` is reverted** (tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:80-88, guarding orca.nix:38)
- The test starts the payload in the background from `bash -c '... &'`, and that shell exits immediately.
- `--die-with-parent` uses `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`, which bwrap sets only once it is running. If the parent is already gone by then, the process has been reparented and the signal never fires.
- The real `orca-ide open` keeps node alive while it waits on profile metadata, which is why the real bug showed up.
- I checked this with bwrap directly, writing no files (stdout piped to `cat`):
  - `bash -c 'bwrap --die-with-parent ... sh -c "sleep 2; echo alive" &'` printed `alive`. That is the same shape as the test, and the payload survived even with die-with-parent on.
  - `bash -c 'bwrap --die-with-parent ... & sleep 0.5'` printed nothing: the payload was killed.
- So the case cannot go red on the regression it claims to catch. The GUI wrapper chain (nixGL, then orca-ide-app, then the FHS launcher) only lengthens the gap.
- Fix: keep the spawning parent alive past bwrap's startup, e.g. `... & sleep 2` inside the `bash -c`, and move the payload's write to about 5s. Then confirm the case goes red with `dieWithParent = true`.

**2. The `orca` symlink goes against upstream and the skills it is meant to serve** (orca.nix:108 and :135; asserted at tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:50-53)
- All six skills say: on Linux outside an Orca terminal use `orca-ide`, and "Never run bare `orca` there", because it is usually the GNOME screen reader.
- Upstream's shim says its Linux name is `orca-ide` to "avoid[] Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict". `serve-app-launcher.js` says "a bare `orca` there is often the screen reader".
- Inside an Orca terminal, Orca's own shim directory supplies `orca`.
- So no skill path in this Linux-only profile reaches `$out/bin/orca`. It can still collide with nixpkgs' `pkgs.orca` (screen reader, also pname `orca`, a buildEnv conflict if it is ever added) or shadow `/usr/bin/orca` depending on PATH order.
- The comment "their name for it elsewhere" is accurate only for macOS/Windows and inside Orca terminals, none of which this binary covers. Consider dropping the link.

**3. Risky third-party text installed globally into every Claude session** (orca.nix:255-258, list at :160-163)
- All six stubs say: "If it fails with `runtime_access_denied`, your sandbox blocked the connection: re-run it with escalated permissions". That tells agents to ask for a sandbox escape, and they do it on Orca's say-so.
- The stubs also tell agents to start the GUI themselves (`ORCA open --json`). With `dieWithParent = false`, that window outlives the agent.
- `computer-use` lets agents drive any visible native window, including external Chrome/Safari with the user's live sessions.
- These are pinned and hash-checked, and the permission system still gates escalation. But they now load in every `~/.claude` session, not only in Orca terminals. That is a deliberate exposure the commit message does not mention.
- `orca-linear` and `linear-tickets` are byte-identical apart from the name. `linear-tickets` is labelled "Legacy bundled name ... kept so existing installs converge", which a fresh Nix install doesn't need. Both also overlap the repo's own `linear-flow` skill (home.nix:2297) on "working from a linked Linear issue", which makes triggering ambiguous. I suggest dropping `linear-tickets` and deciding deliberately about `orca-linear` vs `linear-flow`.

### nit
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:98: the comment is wrong.** "CI's bash is built without programmable completion" is false. `nixpkgs/29916453...#bash` (TOOLS_REV) builds `bash-interactive-5.3p9`, and there both `${!ORCA_@}` and `compgen -v ORCA_` work. `env "${u[@]}"` with an empty array under `set -u` also works there. The code is fine; only the stated reason is wrong.
- **orca.nix:116-117 and tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:64-66: the fallback is described wrongly.** Both say that without `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` the CLI falls back to `process.execPath` (node). Under plain node, `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is unset, so `open` throws `runtime_open_failed` (launch.js) and `serve` is refused outright by `canStartOrcaServer` (serve-app-launcher.js:16-19). The variable is what makes `serve` allowed at all, which the comment doesn't say.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:33 duplicates orca.nix:160-163.** A skill added in orca.nix would go untested. Deriving the list from `home.file` attrNames matching `.claude/skills/` would avoid that.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:83-88: the background payload is never tracked or killed.** It exits itself after 4s. But if node mode were ever not honoured, the test would leave a full GUI window running, and on early `exit 1` paths it may write into the already-deleted `$T`. Capturing the PID and killing it in the EXIT trap would be cleaner.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:131:** `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv"` is unchecked. A failure only shows up later as "$src is missing", which is still a correct FAIL. It also realises the same drv six times.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:123:** `nix eval` stderr is not silenced, so the `recurseIntoAttrs` evaluation warning adds noise to the output. Lines 126/129 already use `2>/dev/null`.

### Checks with no findings
- **Secrets:** `outside()` passes only variable names (`${!ORCA_@}`) to `env -u`. Nothing echoes values, there is no `set -x`, and failure messages print only CLI output. `ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_TOKEN`'s value is never printed.
- **Privacy:** no emails or private data in the diff.
- **Temp dir:** `mktemp -d` plus an EXIT trap (line 27), the same pattern as sandbox-fonts.sh.
- **CI tools:** the script uses only coreutils (mktemp, timeout, seq, paste, tr, sha256sum, uname), grep, sed, jq, nix and nix-store, all supplied by the `nix shell` in nix-eval.yml. No python3 or util-linux.
- **CI GUI case:** the node-mode case runs the GUI under bwrap plus nixGL (mesa) in the privileged container. It needs no GPU or display, but I could not confirm a CI run.
- **CLI on plain node:** the CLI's external requires are only `node:*`, `zod` and `@orca/process-host`. The one native module, sherpa-onnx in serve-speech-recognizer, is loaded by the app side. The bundled Electron reports node 24.22.0, so the "same major" claim holds.
- **NODE_OPTIONS handover** matches upstream's shim exactly.
- **orca.nix code:** the `''${...}` escaping, the column-0 heredoc after Nix's indent stripping, and `placeholder "out"` inside the quoted heredoc are all correct.
- **Desktop entry and sandbox-fonts.sh:** `Exec`/`mainProgram` are updated together. sandbox-fonts.sh's `.*orca-[0-9.]+` filter does not match `orca-cli-1.4.238`, and its `.orca-ide-unwrapped` lookup is unaffected.
- **Other cases fail on their regressions:** bin names, plain node exec, `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` pointing at the nixGL-wrapped GUI, node mode (an always-on flag gives "bad option"), `--version`, `skills get`, exit status 1, rev == `sourceCommit`, and manifest hashes.
- **Rev bump without hash bump:** the rev in the fetch `name` gives a new store path for the fixed-output fetch, so the build fails as the comment claims.
- **Consistency with home.nix:** `home.file` with `"${src}/skills/<name>"` matches the existing `.claude/skills` wiring. The fetch is pinned in the module instead of as a flake input, and the comment explains why.
